title: Prove the height-1 truncated-source count and its endpoint gaps.
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Author-checked identity for the default height-1 slab of the #4470 product/completion/split rule under #4436 nested widths. No new κ and no selected-frontier change. The selected conditional exponent remains `60403/20000000`.

If target multiplicities lie in ranks `[L, m]`, paid ranks satisfy `rmax < L`, and `cap = n//m` satisfies `L <= cap < L^2`, the merged source count is

```text
S = W*A(cap) + P*(W - A(cap)),
```

where `W` is the total target multiplicity, `A(cap)` is the multiplicity of target ranks at most `cap`, and `P` is the total paid multiplicity. Equivalently `S - W^2 = (W - A(cap))*(P - W)`. When `cap >= m`, `S = W^2`.

At the published `v = 1` invoice this is `328391680` at cap 21 and `119421184 = 10928^2` for every cap from 145 through 440. The drop is exactly `(77564-10928)*(10928-7792)`. Because `P > W`, `S` falls as `cap` crosses a target rank, so `S_n` is not monotone inside one height.

Substituting this count does not prove `K/N >= 2944/1000` and does not prove `K/N < 3069/1000`. The certified bracket remains `(2943/1000) N < K < (3070/1000) N`, with `H = 64215200000000` and `N = 2^H`. There are fewer than `63945^1024` height-1 ranks, and that block is disjoint from the top slab (`hlo = 14276389504`).

This is a scoped proof plus exact finite checks. It is not a new supplier, a physical word, or a multiplication theorem.

## Task and overlap

Base `ff3cc58e370d0f678e529246f8c73e8094e18fcf`. Card `selected-stock-envelope`, priority revision 7, scope refined.

Handoff comment 19140126 asked for one uniform truncated-source estimate because `S` drops from `328391680` to `119421184` between ranks 3045 and 63944. On this base, `research/selected-truncated-source-envelope` already proves that uniform census and `K/N < 3070/1000`. This package does not restate that bound. It proves the height-1 collapse, which that census does not state, and the integer fact that the collapse misses both the next lower thousandth (`2944/1000`, from #5026's `Xlo`) and the next upper thousandth (`3069/1000`, from the recomputed moment charge `X = 197115103572543`).

Fork draft: https://github.com/unpaidmoon/integer-mult-bounds/pull/86, head `d7271b4c28911378680c8c1658678ddb4d9b17ae`.

Nearest work: #5026 / `research/selected-complex-width-envelope` and `research/selected-truncated-source-envelope`. Different from unpaidmoon's stock notes on bootstrap floors, `log_q` parents, and joint leaf reserves.

## Validation

Python 3.12, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -W error -B research/height1-truncated-source/verify.py
python3 -I -O -W error -B research/height1-truncated-source/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/height1-truncated-source
```

Registered normal and optimized replay both print `PASS_HEIGHT1_TRUNCATED_SOURCE`. Metadata replay prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/height1-truncated-source outcome=partial`.

The verifier authenticates `flow.py`, the selected invoice, the #5026 receipt and the uniform-moment receipt. It checks 40 small caps, 4 literal replays, all 420 selected height-1 caps, the six published calibration rows, and four rejection controls (paid rank at least `L`, truncated term omitted, extension to `n = 63945`, and a square lower bound where `P < W`). The endpoint gaps are exact integer bit-length comparisons. `N` and the `v = 1024` histogram are not constructed.

Finite checks corroborate the written identity. They are not an enumeration of every rank at `v = 1024`. Not run: an all-height base reduction, exact `B_N`, physical admission, or the selected cold replay.

## Open next questions

The package question is whether a uniform eligible-boundary bound can reduce `log2(T1/L)` by at least three bits on every rank through `N`, enough to replace `3070/1000` by `3069/1000`. The height-1 window cannot do that. The first check is any proposed uniform factor against the `v = 1` count at `n = 63944`. The blocker is a bound that remains valid when a source rank sits just above `n/M`.
